targets.gloss: A jointed or flexible device that allows the pivoting of a door etc.
A wall-mounted socket connected to an electrical power supply, at which current can be taken to run electrical devices.

A hard white translucent ceramic, originally made by firing kaolin, quartz, and feldspar at high temperatures but now also inclusive of similar artificial materials; also often (figurative) such a material as a symbol of the fragility, elegance, etc. traditionally associated with porcelain goods.
Synonym of porcelain, a hard white translucent ceramic made from kaolin, now (chiefly US) sometimes distinguished in reference to tableware as fine or good china.
A flat, rigid structure, fixed at right angles to a wall or forming a part of a cabinet, desk, etc., and used to display, store, or support objects.
An open-topped box that can be slid in and out of the cabinet that contains it, used for storing clothing or other articles.
A cabinet, closet, or other piece of furniture with shelves intended for storing cookware, dishware, or food; similar cabinets or closets used for storing other items.
A movable cupboard or cabinet designed for storing clothes, particularly as a large piece of bedroom furniture.
The overhead closure of a room.
The interior bottom or surface of a house or building; the supporting surface of a room.
A piece of cloth covering a window, bed, etc. to offer privacy and keep out light.
A fabric used as a complete floor covering.
A partial covering for a floor.
A soft mass of material stuffed into a cloth bag, used for comfort or support.
A soft cushion used to support the head in bed.
A heavy, loosely woven fabric, usually large and woollen, used for warmth while sleeping or resting.
A quilt or usually flat cloth bag with a filling (traditionally down) and usually an additional washable cover, used instead of blankets; often called a comforter or quilt, especially in US English.
A pad on which a person can recline and sleep, usually having an inner section of coiled springs covered with foam or other cushioning material then enclosed with cloth fabric.
A washable, easily removable cloth cover for pillows.
A cloth used for wiping, especially one used for drying anything wet, such as a person after a bath.
An exposed plumbing fitting; a tap or spigot; a regulator for controlling the flow of a liquid from a reservoir.
A basin used for holding water for washing.
A large container for holding water in which a person may bathe (take a bath).
A device for bathing by which water is made to fall on the body from a height, either from a tank or by the action of a pump.
A conduit allowing liquid to flow out of an otherwise contained volume; a plughole (UK)
A smooth surface, usually made of glass with reflective material painted on the underside, that reflects light so as to give an image of what is in front of it.
A coarse mat at the entrance to a house, upon which one wipes one's shoes.
A bell, buzzer, or chime device mounted on or adjacent to a door's exterior, meant to be rung by a visitor to announce one's presence.
The lowermost part of a doorway that one crosses to enter; a sill.
A flight of stairs; a stairway.
A fence or barrier consisting of one or more horizontal rails and vertical supports.
The space, often unfinished and with sloped walls, directly below the roof in the uppermost part of a house or other building, generally used for storage or habitation.
A floor of a building below ground level.
An accessible structure extending from a building, especially outside a window.
A vertical tube or hollow column used to emit environmentally polluting gaseous and solid matter (including but not limited to by-products of burning carbon- or hydrocarbon-based fuels); a flue.
An open hearth for holding a fire at the base of a chimney.
A finned metal fixture that carries hot water or steam in order to heat a room.
A device that automatically responds to changes in temperature by activating a heating or cooling system to maintain the temperature at a desired setting.
A device that uses suction, and often agitation, in order to remove dirt and other debris from carpets and hard floors.
A domestic utensil with fibers bound together at the end of a long handle, used for sweeping.
A flat scoop with a handle, into which dust, dirt and other material is conveyed with a brush or broom.
An implement for washing floors or similar, made of a piece of cloth, or a collection of thrums, or coarse yarn, fastened to a handle.
Any non-soap cleaning agent, especially a synthetic surfactant.
A place or room where laundering is done - including, by extension, other forms of laundering than clothes washing.
A clip or fastener used to secure garments to a clothesline while drying, and sometimes for other applications requiring holding or pinching.
Large movable item(s), usually in a room, which enhance(s) the room's characteristics, functionally or decoratively.
A person that leases real property; a lessor.
One who holds a lease (a tenancy).
A payment made by a tenant at intervals in order to lease a property.

A (usually) metal fastener consisting of a partially or completely threaded shank, sometimes with a threaded point, and a head used to both hold the top material and to drive the screw either directly into a soft material or into a prepared hole.
A hand tool or power tool which engages with the head of a screw and allows torque to be applied to turn the screw, thus driving it in or loosening it.

A spike-shaped metal fastener used for joining wood or similar materials. The nail is generally driven through two or more layers of material by means of impacts from a hammer or other device. It is then held in place by friction.
A tool with a heavy head and a handle used for pounding.
A pincer-like gripping tool that multiplies the strength of the user's hand, often used for bending things.
A hand tool for making rotational adjustments, such as fitting nuts and bolts, or fitting pipes.
A tool or machine used to remove material so as to create a hole, typically by plunging a rotating cutting bit into a stationary workpiece.
Such a tool with a toothed blade.
A frame, usually portable, of wood, metal, or rope, used for ascent and descent, consisting of two side pieces to which are fastened rungs (cross strips or rounds acting as steps).
A graduated flexible ribbon used for measuring lengths.
A tool employing a chamber with a colored liquid (usually alcohol, hence spirit) and an air bubble, used to determine a horizontal or vertical reference line.
Strong paper coated with (traditionally) sand or (today) manufactured aluminum oxide, silicon carbide, or other abrasive material, used for smoothing and polishing.
A thin brush for applying paint.
A cylindrical tool for applying paint or ink.
A clear or translucent liquid coating composed of resin dissolved in a solvent, which dries by evaporation to form a hard, protective, and typically glossy finish.
A hard gelatin made by boiling bones and hides, used in solution as an adhesive; or any sticky adhesive substance.
Tape with an adhesive film on one side, used to attach materials to something.

A (usually) metal fastener consisting of a cylindrical body that is threaded, with a larger head on one end. It can be inserted into an unthreaded hole up to the head, with a nut then threaded on the other end; a heavy machine screw.

A piece of hardware, typically metal and typically hexagonal or square in shape, with a hole through it having internal screw threads, intended to be screwed onto a threaded bolt or other threaded shaft.

A flat piece of material, often of metal and often an annulus, placed beneath a nut or at some joint, to distribute pressure, alleviate friction, provide directionally differentiated friction (e.g. making the nut turn counter-clockwise only with difficulty), or prevent leakage.
Metal formed into a thin, even thread, now usually by being drawn through a hole in a steel die.
An assembly of two or more wires, used for electrical power or data circuits; one or more and/or the whole may be insulated.
A pronged connecting device which fits into a mating socket, especially an electrical one.

A device to prevent excessive overcurrent from overload or short circuit in an electrical circuit, containing a component that melts and interrupts the current when too high a load is passed through it.
A rigid tube that transports water, steam, or other fluid, as used in plumbing and numerous other applications.
A crack, crevice, fissure, or hole which admits water or other fluid, or lets it escape.
A tight closure, secure against leakage.
The deteriorated state of iron or steel as a result of moisture and oxidation; it consists mostly of iron(III) oxide (ferric oxide) and iron(II) oxide (ferrous oxide).
A disruption, mark or shallow cut on a surface made by scratching.
A shallow deformation in the surface of an object, produced by an impact.
The sharp sound made when solid material breaks.
The substance making up the central part of the trunk and branches of a tree. Used as a material for construction, to manufacture various items, etc. or as fuel.
Construction material supplied in sheets, and made of three or more layers of wood veneer glued together, laid up with alternating layers having their grain perpendicular to each other.
An artificial metal produced from iron, harder and more elastic than elemental iron; used figuratively as a symbol of hardness.
A reddish-brown metallic chemical element (symbol Cu) with the atomic number 29; also, the metal made up of this element.
A building material created by mixing cement, water, and aggregate such as gravel and sand.
A hardened rectangular block of mud, clay etc., used for building.
A regularly-shaped slab of clay or other material, affixed to cover or decorate a surface, as in a roof-tile, glazed tile, stove tile, carpet tile, etc.
To make tighter.
To make loose.
To supply or substitute an equivalent with.
To restore to good working order, fix, or improve damaged condition; to mend; to remedy.
To put together.
To ascertain the quantity of a unit of material via calculated comparison with respect to a standard.
To connect, set up or prepare something for use
To disconnect from a supply, especially an electrical socket.
Any of a variety of materials designed to reduce the flow of heat, either from or into a building.
An opening into which a plug or other connecting part is designed to fit (e.g. a light bulb socket).
Any of various large coniferous evergreen trees or shrubs from the genus Picea, found in northern temperate and boreal regions; originally and more fully spruce fir.
Any coniferous tree of the genus Pinus.
A deciduous tree with distinctive deeply lobed leaves, acorns, and notably strong wood, typically of England and northeastern North America, included in genus Quercus.
A tree of the genus Fagus having a smooth, light grey trunk, oval, pointed leaves, and many branches.
Any of various trees of the genus Betula, native to countries in the Northern Hemisphere.
Any of various deciduous trees or shrubs in the genus Salix, in the willow family Salicaceae, found primarily on moist soils in cooler zones in the northern hemisphere.

A small tree (Acer campestre), known as the common maple, field maple, or hedge maple, which has palmate leaves with five lobes and winged seeds, and is chiefly native to East Asia, Europe, North Africa, and North America.

An edible nut (technically a fruit) of the Spanish chestnut or sweet chestnut tree (Castanea sativa); also (chiefly preceded by a descriptive word), a nut from a related shrub or tree; or a similar nut from an unrelated plant.
A shade tree of the genus Fraxinus.
A conifer of the genus Abies.
The usually single, more or less upright part of a tree, between the roots and the branches.
The exterior covering of the trunk and branches of a tree or of various other woody plants.
The woody part of a tree arising from the trunk and usually dividing.
A small thin branch of a tree or bush.
The part of a plant, generally underground, that anchors and supports the plant body, absorbs and stores water and nutrients, and in some plants is able to perform vegetative reproduction.
The usually green and flat organ that represents the most prominent feature of most vegetative plants.
A needle-like leaf found on some conifers.
The fruit of a conifer or a similarly shaped fruit or flower head of certain other plants, such as banksias and proteas.
The fruit of the oak, being an oval nut growing in a woody cup or cupule.
Any alga, lichen, bryophyte, or other plant of seemingly simple structure.
Any of a group of some twenty thousand species of vascular plants classified in the division Pteridophyta that lack seeds and reproduce by shedding spores to initiate an alternation of generations.
Any of several woody, climbing, or trailing evergreen plants of the genus Hedera.
A thicket of bushes or other shrubbery, especially one planted as a fence between two portions of land, or to separate the parts of a garden.
A woody plant smaller than a tree, and usually with several stems from the same base.
Any plant unwanted at the place where and at the time when it is growing.
Ground (generally in front of or around a house) covered with grass kept closely mown.
A mixture of mineral particles and organic material, used to support plant growth.
A small stone, especially one rounded by the action of water.
Small fragments of rock, used for laying on the beds of roads and railways, and as ballast.
A field or pasture; a piece of land either intentionally cultivated with grass or (especially) naturally covered with grass, especially one that is intended to be mown for hay or to be grazed.
Ground covered with grass or herbage, used or suitable for the grazing of livestock.
A dense uncultivated tract of trees and undergrowth, larger than woods.
An area of land within a wood or forest devoid of trees.
An inland body of standing water, either natural or man-made, that is smaller than a lake.
A small river; a large creek; a body of moving water confined by banks.
A sloped side of a river acting as a barrier between the water and level ground to either side.
Any of the rodents of the family Sciuridae.
A small mammal of the subfamily Erinaceinae, characterized by their spiny back and often by the habit of rolling up into a ball when attacked, native to Afro-Eurasia.
A ruminant mammal with hooves and often antlers, of the family Cervidae, or one of several similar animals from related families of the order Artiodactyla, such as the musk deer or mouse deer.
Any member of the genus Vulpes; a true fox.
Any member of species of the genera Meles, Arctonyx, Mellivora or Taxidea, of mammals.

Any of various birds of prey of the order Strigiformes, families Strigidae and Tytonidae, that are primarily nocturnal and have forward-looking, binocular vision, limited eye movement, and good hearing.
The house sparrow, Passer domesticus; a small bird with a short bill, and brown, white and gray feathers.
A European robin, Erithacus rubecula.
Any of numerous species of insect in the order Coleoptera characterized by a pair of hard, shell-like front wings which cover and protect a pair of rear wings when at rest.
Any of many types of stinging flying insect resembling a hornet.
The larva of a butterfly or moth; leafworm.
Any of very many animals (either hermaphroditic or nonhermaphroditic), of the class Gastropoda, having a coiled shell.
A worm that lives in the ground.
Any of the several species of plant in the genus Taraxacum, characterised by yellow flower heads and notched, broad-ended leaves, especially the common dandelion (Taraxacum officinale).
Light rain.
A heavy fall of rain.
A brief fall of precipitation (spell of rain, or a similar fall of snow, sleet, or cascade); burst of hefty precipitation.
Balls or pieces of ice falling as precipitation, often in connection with a thunderstorm.
Pellets of ice made of mostly-frozen raindrops or refrozen melted snowflakes.
A cover of minute ice crystals on objects that are exposed to the air. Frost is formed by the same process as dew, except that the temperature of the frosted object is below freezing.
Any moisture from the atmosphere condensed by cool bodies upon their surfaces.
A thick cloud that forms near the ground; the obscurity of such a cloud.
Water or other liquid finely suspended in air. (Compare fog, haze.)
A light, gentle wind.
A strong, abrupt rush of wind.
The loud rumbling, cracking, or crashing sound caused by expansion of rapidly heated air around a lightning bolt.
A flash of light produced by short-duration, high-voltage discharge of electricity within a cloud, between clouds, or between a cloud and the earth.
A period of unusually low rainfall, longer and more severe than a dry spell.
An overflow of a large amount of water (usually disastrous) from a lake or other body of water due to excessive rainfall or other input of water.
Dampness, especially that of the air.
A prediction of the weather.
Covered with clouds; overshadowed; darkened; (meteorology) more than 90% covered by clouds.
Cold enough to cause discomfort.
Moderately warm, especially less cold than expected.
Of a surface, having low friction, often due to being covered in a non-viscous liquid, and therefore hard to grip, hard to stand on without falling, etc.
Covered or splashed with, or full of, mud (“wet soil”).
Of a near-vertical gradient; of a slope, surface, curve, etc. that proceeds upward or downward at an angle approaching vertical.
A surface that either inclines or declines in a regular manner from the perspective of an observer.
A vertical (or nearly vertical) rock face.
An elongated depression cast between hills or mountains, often with a river flowing through it.
A chain of mountains.
The highest point of a hill, mountain, or similar geographical feature.
Land adjoining a non-flowing body of water, such as an ocean, lake or pond.
The daily fluctuation in the level of the sea caused by the gravitational influence of the moon and the sun.
A moving disturbance in the level of a body of liquid; an undulation.
The generally unidirectional movement of a gas or fluid.
A body of water (especially the sea) contained by a concave shoreline.
A piece of land projecting into water from a larger land mass.
A flow of water over the edge of a cliff.
A route for travel over land, especially a narrow, unpaved pathway for use by hikers, horseback riders, etc.
A small, often temporary, pool of water, usually on a path or road.
The time of day when the sun appears above the eastern horizon.
The moment each evening when the sun disappears below the western horizon.
The skeletal joint which connects the foot with the leg; the uppermost portion of the foot and lowermost portion of the leg, which contain this skeletal joint.
The complex joint between forearm bones, carpus, and metacarpals where the hand is attached to the arm; the carpus in a narrow sense.
The joint between the upper arm and the forearm.
The joint between the arm and the torso, sometimes including the surrounding muscles, tendons, and ligaments.
The bottom of a face, (specifically) the typically jutting jawline below the mouth.
One of the bones, usually bearing teeth, which form the framework of the mouth.
The part of the face above the eyebrows and below the hairline.
The hair that grows over the bone ridge above the eye socket.
A thin skin membrane that covers and moves over an eye.
The soft skin on each side of the face, below the eyes; the outer surface of the sides of the oral cavity.
The front part of the neck.
The portion of the human body from the base of the neck to the top of the abdomen; the homologous area in some other animals.
A series of bones situated at the back from the head to the pelvis of a human, or from the head to the tail of an animal, enclosing the spinal cord and providing support for the thorax and abdomen.
Any of a series of long curved bones occurring in 12 pairs in humans and other animals and extending from the spine to or toward the sternum.
The outward-projecting parts of the pelvis and top of the femur and the overlying tissue.
The upper leg of a human, between the hip and the knee.
The back of the leg below the knee.
The rear part of the foot, where it joins the leg.
The shortest and thickest digit of the hand that for humans has the most mobility and can be made to oppose (moved to touch) all of the other fingers.
The inner and somewhat concave part of the human hand or other primate hand that extends from the wrist to the bases of the fingers.
A purplish mark on the skin due to leakage of blood from capillaries under the surface that have been damaged by a blow.
A small bubble between the layers of the skin that contains watery or bloody fluid and is caused by friction and pressure, burning, freezing, chemical irritation, disease, or infection.

An area of inflamed and irritated skin characterized by reddened spots that may be filled with fluid or pus. Also, preceded by a descriptive word (rare or obsolete), an illness characterized by a type of rash.
An injury, such as a cut, stab, or tear, to a (usually external) part of the body.
A permanent mark on the skin, sometimes caused by the healing of a wound.
The act or result of spraining; lameness caused by spraining
A painful contraction of a muscle which cannot be controlled; (sometimes) a similar pain even without noticeable contraction.
The state of being swollen.
A feeling of illness or discomfort in the digestive system, usually characterized by a strong urge to vomit.
The state of being dizzy; the sensation of instability.
A higher than normal body temperature of a person (or, generally, a mammal), usually caused by disease.
A sudden, often involuntary expulsion of air from the lungs through the glottis (causing a short, explosive sound), and out through the mouth.
To expel air as a reflex induced by an irritation in the nose.
A sensation felt on an area of the skin that causes a person or animal to want to scratch said area.
Causing pain or discomfort; painfully sensitive.
Rigid; hard to bend; inflexible.
Physically unable to feel, not having the power of sensation.
A strip of gauze or similar material used to protect or support a wound or injury.
A viscous preparation of oils and/or fats, usually containing medication, used as a treatment or as an emollient.
A written order from an authorized medical practitioner for provision of a medicine or other treatment, such as (ophthalmology) the specific lenses needed for a pair of glasses.
A drug that numbs the pain in the body.
An arrangement between people to meet; an engagement.
A routine visit to the doctor, dentist, or the like.

A disorder of the immune system causing adverse reactions to substances (allergens) not harmful to most and marked by the body's production of histamines and associated with atopy, anaphylaxis, and asthma; any condition of hypersensitivity to a substance.

A perceived change in some function, sensation or appearance of a person that indicates a disease or disorder, such as fever, headache or rash; strictly, a symptom is felt or experienced by the patient, while a sign can be detected by an observer.
The part of a garment that covers the arm.
The part of an upper garment (shirt, jacket, etc.) that fits around the neck and throat, especially if sewn from a separate piece of fabric.
The end of a shirt sleeve that covers the wrist.
An utterance or sound of the voice like "hem", often indicative of hesitation or doubt, sometimes used to call attention.
A folded-back and stitched piece of fabric; especially, the stitching that joins two or more pieces of fabric.
A covering for the inside surface of something.
A zip fastener.
A knob or disc that is passed through a loop or (buttonhole), serving as a fastener.

A metal clasp with a hinged tongue or a spike through which a belt or strap is passed and penetrated by the tongue or spike, in order to fasten the ends of the belt together or to secure the strap to something else.
A lace used for fastening a shoe.
The bottom of a shoe or boot.
The inside sole of a shoe or other footwear.
A bag stitched to an item of clothing, used for carrying small items.
A band of fabric encircling the waist, especially a part of a pair of pants or a skirt.
A band worn around the waist to hold clothing to one's body (usually pants), hold weapons (such as a gun or sword), or serve as a decorative piece of clothing.
A long, often knitted, garment worn around the neck.
A cap that fits the head closely, usually knitted from wool.
A type of sweater or jumper that fastens up the front with buttons or a zipper, usually machine- or hand-knitted from wool.
A loose shirt, usually made of a knit fleece, for athletic wear and now often used as casual apparel.
A waterproof coat to be worn in the rain; (loosely) any coat or jacket with this purpose.
A set of clothes to be worn together, now especially a man's matching jacket and trousers (also business suit or lounge suit), or a similar outfit for a woman.
An ornamental garment worn under a doublet.
A close-fitting, sheer or non-sheer skin-tight garment worn principally by women and girls that covers the body completely from the waist down, usually including the feet.
A plant of genus Gossypium, used as a source of such fiber.
The hair of the sheep, llama and some other ruminants.
Thread or cloth made from flax fiber.
A fine fiber excreted by the silkworm or other arthropod (such as a spider).
A tough material produced from the skin of animals, by tanning or similar process, used e.g. for clothing; often denotes leather from cattle when no qualifier specifies otherwise.
A type of soft leather, made from calfskin, with a brushed texture to resemble fabric, often used to make boots, clothing and fashion accessories.
A closely woven fabric (originally of silk, now also of cotton or man-made fibres) with a thick short pile on one side.
Having stripes, decorated or marked with bands differing in color.
Having a pattern of checks; checkered.
Uneven, with many furrows and prominent points, often in reference to the skin or hide of animals.
A discolored spot or area caused by spillage or other contact with certain fluids or substances.
A bowl-shaped kitchen utensil with holes in it used for draining food that has been cooking in water, such as pasta.
A device with a mesh, grate, or otherwise perforated bottom to separate, in a granular material, larger particles from smaller ones, or to separate solid objects from a liquid.
A kitchen utensil, now usually made from stiff wire loops fixed to a handle (and formerly of twigs), used for whipping (or a mechanical device with the same function).
A kitchen utensil consisting of a flat surface attached to a long handle, used for turning, lifting, or stirring food.
A deep-bowled spoonlike utensil with a long, usually curved, handle.
a tool with which one grates, especially foods such as cheese, to facilitate getting small particles or shreds off a solid lump
A household utensil for peeling fruit or vegetables.
Synonym of cutting board.
A deep cooking vessel with a long protruding handle and sometimes a lid; used for boiling, stewing and making sauces.
A long-handled, shallow pan used for frying food.
The top or cover of a container.
A vessel or appliance used to boil water for the preparation of hot beverages and other foodstuffs.
A chamber used for baking or heating.
A device for heating food, (UK) a cooker.
An oven-proof metal tray used to hold foods in the oven.
A thick, malleable substance made by mixing flour with other ingredients such as water, eggs, or butter, that is made into a particular form and then baked.
A beaten mixture of flour and liquid (usually egg and milk), used for baking (e.g. pancakes, cake, or Yorkshire pudding) or to coat food (e.g. fish) prior to frying.
A single-celled fungus of any of a wide variety of taxonomic families.
Powder obtained by grinding or milling cereal grains, especially wheat, or other foodstuffs such as soybeans and potatoes, and used to bake bread, cakes, and pastry.
Carbohydrates, as with grain and potato based foods.
A sour liquid formed by the fermentation of alcohol used as a condiment or preservative; a dilute solution of acetic acid.
A soup made from broth and other ingredients such as vegetables, herbs or diced meat.
A dark savoury sauce prepared from stock and usually meat juices; brown gravy.
An allocated amount.
The action of squeezing a small amount of a person's skin and flesh, making it hurt.
One of the small bulbs that make up the large, compound bulb in garlic, shallots, or similar plants.
To remove the skin or outer covering of.
To cut into pieces with short, vigorous cutting motions.
To cut into slices.
To cut into small cubes.
To shred (things, usually foodstuffs), by rubbing across a grater.
To disturb the relative position of the particles (of a liquid or similar) by passing an object through it.
To mix in a rapid aerating fashion, especially food.
To work and press into a mass, usually with the hands; especially, to work, as by repeated pressure with the knuckles, into a well mixed mass, the materials of bread, cake, etc.
To cook or undergo heating slowly at or below the boiling point.
To heat to the point where it begins to turn into a gas.
To cook food by heating in an oven or over a fire without covering, resulting in a crisp, possibly even slightly charred appearance.
To cook (something) in an oven (for someone).
To cook with steam.
To gradually cause (something frozen, such as earth, ice, or snow) to melt or soften by raising the temperature.
To flavour food with spices, herbs or salt.
Of a fruit, vegetable, seed, etc., ready for reaping or gathering; having attained perfection; mature.
No longer fresh, in reference to food, urine, straw, wounds, etc.
Lacking in taste or flavor.
Either salty or spicy, but not sweet.
Having an acrid taste (usually from a basic substance).
Made rancid by fermentation, etc.
Likely to crunch, especially with reference to food when it is eaten.
A concrete margin along the edge of a road; a kerb (UK, Australia, New Zealand).
A paved footpath located at the side of a road, for the use of pedestrians.
A point designated for pedestrians to cross a street.
The junction of two (or more) paths, streets, highways, or other thoroughfares.
A road junction at which traffic streams circularly around a central island.
A lengthwise division of roadway intended for a single line of vehicles.
A usually unsealed strip of land bordering a road, where vehicles can drive or park in an emergency.
A shallow pit or other edged depression in a road's surface, especially when caused by erosion, weather or traffic.
A diversion or deviation from one's original route.
A fee paid for some liberty or privilege, particularly for the privilege of passing over a bridge or on a highway, or for that of vending goods in a fair, market, etc.
A situation in which road traffic accumulates until it is stationary or very slow.
The maximum speed permitted by law for vehicles.
The right to proceed first in traffic, on land, on water or in the air. Also in metaphorical senses.
An identifying tag, usually made of metal, bearing a sequence of letters or numbers identifying the vehicle, and placed at the rear and, often, also at the front of a motor vehicle.
A transparent screen made of glass, located at the front and back of a vehicle in front of its occupants to protect them from the wind force generated by the vehicle's speed and inclement weather.
Something, such as a windscreen wiper, that is designed for wiping.
A panel beneath the windshield of a vehicle or aircraft containing indicator gauges, compartments, and sometimes controls and indicator lights.
A wheel-shaped control that is rotated by the driver to steer, existing in most modern land vehicles.
A configuration of the transmission of a motor car so as to achieve a particular ratio of engine to axle torque.
A device to interrupt power transmission, commonly used to separate the engine and gearbox in a car.

A device used to slow or stop the motion of a wheel, or of a vehicle, usually by friction (although other resistive forces, such as electromagnetic fields or aerodynamic drag, can also be used); also, the controls or apparatus used to engage such a mechanism such as the pedal in a car.
A pedal causing the vehicle to accelerate when it is pressed.
A bright light, with a lens and reflector, on the front of a motor vehicle (or originally a ship or train), designed to illuminate the road when driving at night; normally one of a pair.
A turn signal; each of the flashing lights on each side of a vehicle which indicate a turn is being made to left or right, or a lane change etc.
Parts at the front and back of a vehicle which are meant to absorb the impact of a collision; fender.
The luggage storage compartment of a sedan/saloon-style car.
The hinged cover over the engine of a motor vehicle, known as a bonnet in other countries.
US and Canada spelling of tyre: The rubber covering on a wheel.
Used other than figuratively or idiomatically: see spare, tire.

targets.de: Bei he, she und it steht does. Das Vollverb bleibt in der Grundform.
Nach did steht das Vollverb in der Grundform, auch bei unregelmäßigen Verben.
In der einfachen Gegenwart erhält das Verb bei he, she und it normalerweise die Endung -s oder -es.
Die Verlaufsform besteht aus am, is oder are und der -ing-Form.
Unregelmäßige Verben haben eigene Vergangenheitsformen. Diese Aufgabe beschreibt ein abgeschlossenes Ereignis.
Das Present perfect wird mit have oder has und dem Partizip gebildet.
For bezeichnet eine Dauer; since nennt den Zeitpunkt, an dem etwas begonnen hat.
Das Past perfect besteht aus had und dem Partizip. Es beschreibt ein Ereignis vor einem anderen vergangenen Ereignis.
Used to mit der Grundform beschreibt frühere Gewohnheiten oder Zustände, die heute nicht mehr gelten.
Nach am/is/are going to folgt die Grundform des Verbs.
In dieser Form des First conditional steht nach if das Present simple; im Hauptsatz steht will mit der Grundform.
Bei einer gedachten oder unwahrscheinlichen Situation steht hier im if-Satz eine Vergangenheitsform und im Hauptsatz would mit der Grundform.
Would have mit Partizip beschreibt hier ein vorgestelltes Ergebnis in der Vergangenheit.
Nach can, could, should, must und might steht das Vollverb ohne to in der Grundform.
Should have mit Partizip drückt aus, was rückblickend besser gewesen wäre.
In indirekten Fragen folgt auf das Fragewort die normale Satzstellung: Subjekt vor Verb.
Nach diesen Verben oder Präpositionen steht die Objektform: me, him, her, us oder them.
Wenn das Nomen nicht erneut genannt wird, stehen eigenständige Possessivpronomen wie mine, yours, hers oder ours.
Reflexivpronomen beziehen sich auf das Subjekt. Hier stimmen Person und Zahl mit dem Subjekt überein.

targets.de: Many steht bei zählbaren Substantiven im Plural. Much steht bei unzählbaren Substantiven.
A few steht bei zählbaren Dingen im Plural. A little steht bei unzählbaren Mengen.
In diesen verneinten Sätzen wird any für eine unbestimmte Menge verwendet.
Wenn nach enjoy eine Tätigkeit folgt, steht das nächste Verb in der -ing-Form.
Nach want folgt für eine gewünschte Tätigkeit to mit der Grundform.
Manche Verben werden in einer bestimmten Bedeutung mit einer festen Präposition verbunden: depend on, listen to, wait for, belong to und apologize for.
Who bezieht sich in diesen Relativsätzen auf eine Person und übernimmt die Rolle des Subjekts.
Nach einem Komparativ steht beim direkten Vergleich than.
Das Passiv besteht aus einer Form von be und dem Partizip des Vollverbs.
Enough steht nach dem Adjektiv, wenn es ausdrückt, dass eine Eigenschaft in ausreichendem Maß vorhanden ist.
